title: Bridlepath deploy slate and telemetry tuning notes
body:
Purpose

Quick, pragmatic deploy slate for the Bridlepath feature bundle + a compact telemetry tuning checklist. Goal: ship a low-risk, observable rollout that lets us iterate on throughput/latency guardrails without alarming SRE or customers. This doc is a working field notebook — not the final runbook.

Summary of what Bridlepath touches
- Model routing adjustments (new fallback weight for small-batch latencies)
- Autoscaler policy change for dedicated pools (scale-down grace = 90s -> 180s)
- New runtime flag to enable warm-kv cache priming for certain large-seq requests
- Minor console route for devs: /v1/bridlepath-preview (internal)

High-level rollout approach
- Canary cohort 1: internal traffic only (team + beta orgs) — 2 hours baseline profiling
- Canary cohort 2: 5% of non-enterprise hosted traffic (region: us-west1) — 4 hours sampling
- Ramp: 5% -> 20% -> 50% over 24–48h depending on telemetry signals
- Optional auto-abort to fallback model variant on signal breach (latency p95 > 450ms or error rate > 0.6%)

Preflight checklist (action owners in parens)
[ ] Merge gating PRs, confirm image tags (Michael)
[ ] Stage smoke deployment in staging with production-like load (Aisha)
[ ] Validate canary routing policy in canary-env (Samira)
[ ] Load KV-cache priming script and test with short and long sequences (Michael)
[ ] Confirm burst tokens budget and quota for trial orgs (platform-ops)
[ ] Update console route docs + mark as internal (docs)
[ ] Create temporary alert channel #deploy-bridlepath (Riley)

Telemetry tuning checklist (why each matters and quick thresholds)
- Latency (p50/p95/p99): baseline is current prod for model X. Target: p95 < 350ms for small sequences; p99 < 900ms. If p95 drift > 25% from baseline -> pause ramp.
- Error rate: track 5xx and user-facing structured errors. Threshold: > 0.6% 5xx sustained for 10m -> abort.
- Token throughput per GPU: watch for sudden drop (sign of bad batching) — if throughput drops > 30% compared to previous 1h median -> revert flag.
- KV cache hit rate: should improve or stay flat. If hit rate drops by > 10% after priming -> investigate cache sharding.
- Latency tail correlated with small-batch scheduling: add tag to samples identify batch_size <= 4; expected p95 for those to be better than medium batches after priming.

Quick signal queries (ops snippets)
- p95 latency: metrics.query("latency.p95{route:bridlepath-preview}")
- 5xx rate: metrics.query("errors.count{route:bridlepath-preview}/requests.count{route:bridlepath-preview}")
- KV hit: metrics.query("kv.cache.hit_rate{pool:bridlepath}")
- Batching histogram: logs.search("batch_size:<n> route:bridlepath-preview")
(we'll paste concrete dashboards here once reviewed)

Rollout calendar (compact)
2026-10-06 09:00 PT: Canary 1 deploy (internal) — smoke + 2h profile
2026-10-06 12:30 PT: Decision checkpoint — proceed? (if all green -> cohort 2)
2026-10-06 13:00 PT: Canary 2 deploy to us-west1 @ 5% traffic
2026-10-06 17:00 PT: Checkpoint — evaluate telemetry (4h sample window)
2026-10-07 09:00 PT: Ramp to 20% (if green) with 6h watch
2026-10-07 18:00 PT: Decision — continue to 50% or hold for 24h

Rollback and escape hatch (explicit criteria)
- Immediate rollback (manual): any sustained customer-facing error reports for production SKU or rollback toggle triggered by oncall.
- Auto-fallback: if p95 > 450ms for 10m AND 5xx > 0.6% -> route traffic to model-bridlepath-fallback variant (automated).
- Graceful degrade path: shift non-critical routes to lower-cost variant and preserve enterprise SLOs.

Release notes (draft)
- Feature: Bridlepath routing improves small-sequence latency by enabling targeted KV priming and adjusted batching heuristics.
- Behavior change: Dedicated autoscaler scale-down grace increased to reduce thrash for bursts; customers on Dedicated may see slightly higher short-term capacity retention.
- Admins: New internal preview route /v1/bridlepath-preview for testing.
- Rollout: phased, beginning with internal canary then gradual ramp in us-west1.
- Caveats: May slightly increase short-term costs in Dedicated pools while autoscaler settles.

Open questions / decisions to make before public release
- Do we expose priming toggle to Dedicated customers? (Prod-safety vs. control)
- Throttle policy for orgs historically close to quota — should we exclude them during 5% stage?
- Long-term: should priming be adaptive (per-tenant) or global? Perf vs. implementation complexity.

Post-deploy retro prompts (fill-in in 48–72h post-roll)
- Signals that predicted success vs. surprises (compare preflight expectations to results)
- Operator friction: did any manual intervention feel avoidable? Where to add automation?
- Cost impact: short-term vs. 7-day trend — any need for cost mitigations?
- Customer impact: any user-facing degradation or confusion?

Notes to self / quick hacks
- If KV hit rate lags, try priming list: top-50 prefixes for orgs with high sequence lengths. Script at: github links above.
- If batch scheduler starvation observed, temporarily adjust max_batch_wait_ms by +10ms and evaluate.
- Keep one SRE oncall in the channel for first 12h of ramp.

Slack & comms
- Preflight ping: #release-readout at +30m before canary 1
- Live channel for rollout: #deploy-bridlepath (archive after 72h)
- Customer comms: internal CS note template in Confluence -> link in linked_artifacts when ready.

Appendix: quick checklist for 0–6h after canary 2 (shorthand for ops)
- 0m: deploy -> verify pod readiness -> sanity checks pass (health endpoints)
- 10m: smoke traffic test (synthetic short seq / long seq)
- 30m: kv hit rate baseline vs. staging -> +/-%
- 60m: p95 latency check for small batches
- 120m: detailed histogram export + initial decision

This is intentionally concise; expand into a full runbook if we go beyond 50% traffic. For now: keep it light, observable, and reversible.

Riley T. (oncall lead for first 24h)
